title: Rivergate and Trail
premise: Mirabel Vane has spent nine years running cargo up the Rivergate, keeping her boat, the Sparrowhawk, moving because every stop risks someone learning what she did at Trail's Landing. When her old rival Cassian Roe hires her crew to salvage a sunken pay-barge above the Landing itself — the one stretch of river she swore off — she takes the job anyway, because his money can save her leaking hull and her stranded crew's wages. But the wreck holds more than coin: it holds proof that the flood that drowned Trail's Landing was no accident, and that Mirabel's own father helped open the sluice gates. As the monsoon rises and Roe's backers close in to destroy the evidence, Mirabel must choose between protecting her name and giving the Landing's survivors the truth they've waited nine years for. She scuttles the barge's ledger into safe hands, loses the Sparrowhawk to the flood, and finally stops running — taking a berth as pilot on the rebuilt Landing ferry, where belonging costs everything but pays daily.
about_author: Ada Eastwick is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent six seasons charting commercial waterways before turning to fiction full-time. Her novels are known for their brackish moral weather and characters who treat geography like family history.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Mirabel pilots the Sparrowhawk through low water, establishing her intimate knowledge of the Rivergate and her restless refusal to dock anywhere long. Crew member Odji presses her about why she never stops at Trail's Landing; she deflects with a story that isn't true. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of constant motion.

chapters.title: A Letter in Wax
chapters.summary: At a mid-river trading post, Mirabel receives Cassian Roe's offer: triple wages to salvage a pay-barge sunk above Trail's Landing before monsoon season seals the upper gorge. Her first mate Tamsin argues the money could recaulk the hull; Mirabel refuses. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread surfacing from old memory, pride versus survival.

chapters.title: What the Hull Confesses
chapters.summary: The shipwright condemns the Sparrowhawk's seams — she cannot make another season without major repairs Mirabel cannot afford. A stranger, Ilan Reyes, a cartographer mapping the changing river, offers to fund repairs in exchange for passage into the gorge. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: cornered pragmatism; the river itself turning against her.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Mirabel negotiates with Ilan, sensing he knows more about Trail's Landing than he admits. She accepts Roe's contract after all, telling herself it's only business. The crew loads salvage gear under gathering storm clouds. POV: Mirabel, with a brief Ilan interlude. Emotional beat: self-deception hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Upstream of Everything
chapters.summary: The ascent into the gorge; Mirabel navigates water she hasn't touched in nine years, and the landscape triggers fragments of memory — a burning warehouse, a gate, her father's hands on a wheel. Ilan watches her too closely. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the past becoming physical, geography as accusation.

chapters.title: Trail's Landing, Half-Drowned
chapters.summary: They moor near the ruined town. Survivors still live there in stilt houses, including Maren Oduya, who recognizes Mirabel and spits at her name. The crew learns the locals call the pay-barge 'the coffin.' POV: alternating Mirabel and Tamsin. Emotional beat: shame made public; hostility that carries grief beneath it.

chapters.title: The Coffin Below
chapters.summary: First dive on the wreck. They find the hold sealed from the inside — someone locked it deliberately. Ilan photographs not gold but an iron strongbox stamped with the Rivergate Authority's seal. Roe's foreman, Brack, orders it left. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: creeping suspicion; the job curdling.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Water
chapters.summary: Maren confronts Mirabel at night, forcing out the shared history: the flood, the dead, the rumor that a Vane opened the gates. Mirabel neither confirms nor denies. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; two women circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Brack's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tensions aboard: Brack secretly radios Roe's backers, reporting the strongbox. Mirabel catches him and realizes the salvage was never about coin — Roe wants whatever the Authority buried. First monsoon rains arrive early. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: betrayal recognized; the trap closing.

chapters.title: What Her Father Opened
chapters.summary: Ilan reveals himself: his brother died in the flood, and he's spent years tracing the Authority's records. He shows Mirabel documents naming her father as the engineer who ordered the sluice opened — under written orders from above. POV: Ilan. Emotional beat: devastating context; Mirabel's inheritance rewritten.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Against Brack's orders, Mirabel and Ilan raise the strongbox at night. Inside: the Authority's ledger proving the flood was deliberate — insurance fraud dressed as engineering failure, with Roe's name among the signatories. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the past fully surfaced.

chapters.title: Roe Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Cassian Roe arrives by steam launch with hired men, all courtesy and menace. He offers Mirabel a fortune to hand over the ledger and forget Trail's Landing again — the same bargain, he notes, her father took. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy; the corruption theme made personal.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits in earnest. The Sparrowhawk drags anchor; half the crew sides with Brack, wanting the payout. Tamsin stays loyal. In the chaos, Brack steals the ledger and rows for Roe's launch. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by fear; the crew fracturing.

chapters.title: Chase in the Gorge
chapters.summary: Mirabel runs the flooded rapids in the leaking Sparrowhawk to intercept Brack — a run she alone can make. They catch the rowboat at Widow's Teeth, but Brack has already passed the ledger to Roe's launch, which turns downstream. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: mastery and desperation fused; her skill as her last honest asset.

chapters.title: Sinking Ground
chapters.summary: The Sparrowhawk takes fatal water. Mirabel beaches her on a sandbar she knows by heart, saving crew and supplies but losing the boat — her home, her name, her escape. She weeps for the first time in the book. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: loss of the thing that let her keep running.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of Stilts
chapters.summary: The survivors of Trail's Landing take the crew in during the worst of the storm. Maren, seeing Mirabel without her boat, offers grudging shelter and hears the whole truth about her father — including that he tried to close the gates and was overruled. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: hospitality as grace; memory corrected, not erased.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Road
chapters.summary: Ilan decodes the ledger's shipping marks: copies were sent to a downstream magistrate who was paid to bury them — but one set went to a widow in Rivergate City, unclaimed. If they can reach her before Roe's lawyers, the truth stands in court. POV: Ilan. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline; purpose replacing revenge.

chapters.title: Downstream, Running Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel borrows Maren's flat-bottomed ferry and races the flood crest downstream, outmaneuvering Roe's launch through channels only she reads correctly. Roe nearly capsizes; Mirabel chooses to throw him a line rather than let him drown. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: power refused its cruelest use; mercy as strength.

chapters.title: The Widow's Door
chapters.summary: In Rivergate City, they find the widow — the Authority clerk's wife — who kept her husband's copy hidden for nine years out of fear. Confronted with Maren's testimony and the drowned town's faces, she surrenders it. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: ordinary courage; memory kept alive by the powerless.

chapters.title: High Water at the Courthouse
chapters.summary: Roe's backers move to seize the evidence through courts and bribes; the magistrate who buried the original docket recuses himself under pressure. The documents go public instead — printed and read aloud on the levee steps as the flood peaks below. POV: Ilan. Emotional beat: climax of exposure; truth outrunning money by inches.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Roe is arrested; Brack vanishes upstream. The Authority collapses into receivership, and reparations are promised to Trail's Landing. Mirabel testifies about her father, clearing his name partially and accepting her own years of silence as a cost she chose. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution; grief given shape.

chapters.title: Rivergate and Trail
chapters.summary: Spring after the monsoon: Mirabel takes the pilot's berth on the new Trail's Landing ferry, running a fixed route between the Landing and Rivergate — stopping, at last, on purpose. She names the ferry for the Sparrowhawk. Maren waves her in from the dock. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, motion transformed into return.
